extracted.intended_audience: Masters of hounds, huntsmen, breeders, and foxhunting enthusiasts
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on the desired conformation, temperament, feeding, training, and management of fell (hill) foxhounds, and how to judge suitability for fell-country hunting. Emphasises working utility over show-type appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fell hound general specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Light in frame, and particularly well let-down and developed in hind quarters. Hare-footed, as opposed to the round cat-foot of the standard type. Good neck, shoulders and loin, long in pastern, and ribs carried well back. A good nose, plenty of tongue, and last, but by no means least, pace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph serves as the core specification for a fell hound — emphasise lightness, strong hindquarters, long pasterns, well-carried ribs, scenting ability, voice and pace. The list should be treated as an integrated set of working traits rather than show-only attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound feet (hare-foot) and dew-claw usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: On the fells the natural or hare-foot is universal. Possessed of a lengthy surface, weight is evenly distributed... Such a foot gets a firm grip on rocks, and offers a smooth surface to the ground on steep descents. In most kennels, the dew-claws are removed from the puppies when the latter are quite young. The fell hounds, however, retain this claw, and it is properly developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound hare- or semi-hare feet are essential for grip, wear distribution and survival on crags; avoid round 'cat-feet' that cramp and knuckle. Retain and develop dew-claws for pulling on slippery rocks — evidence of wear under the nail is proof they are functional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cat-footed (fashionable) type for fell country
rubrics_metrics.description: A hound of the exclusive type is absolutely unsuited to such a country... His round, over-developed, and practically malformed feet... His short, straight pasterns, and round cat-feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the Peterborough/show or 'exclusive' type as an anti-pattern for fell hunting: heavy weight, short pasterns, malformed feet, lack of tongue and inability to work a cold drag all reduce utility and increase maintenance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal height and weight
rubrics_metrics.description: A fell hound should stand under, rather than over, 22½ inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller, lighter-built hounds clear stone walls and steep ground with less strain, experience less jar on landing, fatigue less over a long day, and have longer working careers than larger, heavier hounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-coupled, compact build for jumping
rubrics_metrics.description: To jump properly a hound should be short-coupled, compact in build, and have his ribs carried well back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short coupling allows hind legs to come well under the body, enabling easier clearance of obstacles and reduced landing shock. Prefer compact proportions for agility on steep terrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forelimb angulation and scapula placement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the humerus or bone of the upper arm is nearly in a straight line with the ulna and radius, the pace of the hound will be much greater... To reduce jar to a minimum the scapula should lie well back, in an oblique position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humerus/radius alignment for stride length (near-straight favors pace but increases shock). Ensure scapula set lies back to minimise concussion transmitted to the brain; balance stride/power with shock reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hindquarter conformation and power
rubrics_metrics.description: In the same way with regard to the hind leg, the longer the femur the lower the hock, and the greater the speed... The more obtuse the angle between the femur and tibia, the more power there is to bring the hind legs well under the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge hindquarters for femur length, hock placement, second-thigh muscular development and inside-leg muscle. These determine spring, propulsion and ability to clear banks and walls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cow-hocks (hind limb deviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency towards 'cow hocks,' i.e. a deviation from the straight line between the hock and ground, should be condemned. A 'cow-hocked' hound lifts his hind quarters higher than he should at each stride...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condemn cow-hocked conformation; it indicates shortened tendons, reduced flexion and consequent loss of spring and propulsive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nose / scenting power is paramount
rubrics_metrics.description: Having mentioned some of the more important parts of a fell hound’s anatomy, we may turn to his nose, or scenting power. The latter is the most important quality in a fell hound, for no matter how well-built he is, without nose his utility is nil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise scenting ability above aesthetic traits. A hound must be able to work cold drags and detect stale trails; breeding and training should favour and develop this capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pace, drive and courage (speed with stamina)
rubrics_metrics.description: To press a fox in the rough fell country hounds must have pace, drive, and courage to an unusual degree... such a hound will drive ahead at a tremendous pace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both top speed and sustained drive; a fell hound needs the combination to force foxes from difficult ground. Do not assume pace must come at expense of nose — both can coexist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music (voice) and audibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Next to nose, however, music is most important. Even if you cannot see hounds, yet can hear them plainly, you know what to do, and which direction to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise clear voice so huntsmen can locate hounds at long distances on the fells. Light colouring helps visual contact, but music guides action when hounds are out of sight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light coat colour for visibility on hills
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of the fell hounds are light-coloured; some of them practically white. This is a decided advantage on the hills, where it is impossible to keep in close touch with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer lighter colours to increase visibility against heather and rock during fell hunting; this is a practical safety and management consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breed hounds suited to particular country ('hounds for countries')
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it not equally necessary... for the hounds to be of a type most suited to the requirements of their particular country?... 'hounds for countries' should be the breeders' motto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and judge hounds by suitability to terrain and method of hunting rather than by a universal show standard. Breeding for utility in local conditions yields better long-term sport and durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility over fashion: show standards vs working conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Working ability should be the main object of the man who breeds for sport... It is much better to do this than allow the beauty standard... to take preference of working capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prioritising show competition traits that harm field performance. Judges and breeders should consider awarding by country-type suitability to incentivise working breeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding: use 'stiff' (solid) food, avoid sloppy slop
rubrics_metrics.description: A great deal too much 'slop' is fed to hounds in some kennels... Fed with solid food early the day before hunting, hounds should be fit to run their best on arrival at the meet. Hounds well fed with good stiff food will work better...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feed solid (thicker) food to maintain condition, protect nostrils/eyes from irritation, and prevent digestive/respiratory problems. Time feeding so hounds are fit on the hunt day; avoid sloppy feed that causes nasal/eye irritation and skin problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard feed safeguards skin and teeth; prevents eczema/mange
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard feed not only ensures condition, but is a safeguard against eczema. Sloppy food induces the latter, and without a doubt aggravates mange. Hard food is better for the teeth...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide hard/chewy rations as part of routine feeding to improve dental health, stimulate saliva, and reduce skin maladies associated with sloppy diets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hunt and age-related feeding management
rubrics_metrics.description: On the return from hunting it is... bad policy to allow hounds to absolutely gorge themselves, just a nice feed being much better... Old hounds... should, with advancing years, be fed lighter than was the case in their younger days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent gorging after hunts to avoid indigestion; reduce caloric intake for aging hounds to prevent internal fat that impairs wind and burst capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puppy walking, early exposure and behavioural conditioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The fell hound, like his relations in the Shires, is sent out to walk as a puppy... The majority of fell hounds are walked at farmhouses, where they are assured of sufficient liberty, and become accustomed to knocking about amongst sheep, thus quickly learning that mutton on the hoof is strictly taboo...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use farm walks and shepherds' environments to socialise puppies, habituate them to sheep (prevent mutton-chasing), expose them to hares to develop nose and hunting style, and to develop independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let 'em alone' principle to build perseverance and self-reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Hunting on the fells necessitates practising the 'let 'em alone principle,' for throughout the majority of runs hounds do all their own work unaided by their huntsman. Thus they learn perseverance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow hounds space to work unaided wherever appropriate so they develop independent trailing skills and perseverance needed for long, solitary work on fell terrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cull or remove hounds that worry sheep (behavioral intolerance)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one temptation to which fell hounds are more liable to fall than low-country hounds, i.e. sheep worrying... When this happens the huntsman is reluctantly forced to put down the culprits... Death is the only cure for a hound which takes a liking to mutton on the hoof...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat persistent sheep-worrying as irredeemable behavioural fault; such hounds cannot be trusted and must be removed to protect stock and the pack's utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardiness through natural conditions and frequent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Owing to financial considerations, the fell packs are small, therefore individual hounds have to take the field much oftener... They are kept, too, under less artificial conditions, and in consequence are quite able to run up for many seasons, and are seldom sick or sorry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer conditioning practices that expose hounds to real field work rather than artificial confinement; frequent, natural exercise develops durability and reduces complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and development of scenting through breeding and independent work
rubrics_metrics.description: The reason why the fell hounds possess great scenting power is because of the way they are bred, and also owing to the fact that they do practically all their work unaided, and thus become persevering and absolutely self-reliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breed from and select hounds that demonstrate independent trailing and nose; allow hunting methods that encourage individual development of scenting skills (e.g., lone hunting, long drags).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging emphasis: hindquarters and hind feet over forelimbs
rubrics_metrics.description: In judging the appearance of a hound from a utility view-point, many people are apt to pay much more attention to the fore limbs than the hind. This is a great mistake... pace, freedom of action, and power to overcome obstacles... are much more dependent on the hind limbs than the fore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a hound for fell work, prioritise evaluation of hindquarters, hock, second thigh and hind feet. Forelimb conformation matters, but hind power is primary for jumping and propulsion.
